findings.title: Refusal message at libexec/orchid-start:551 still states the pre-T002 premise ("task files reach the integration branch only through 'orchid plan apply'"); in the helper's declined shapes with no plan on the branch (e.g. an operator who merged a planless $integ into their own branch mid-planning) the refusal fires with that untrue premise and a `run resume`/`run new` recovery that does not apply — the surrounding comments were corrected but the operator-facing string was not

`_start_tasks_inherited` proxies the init-time fork point with the operator's *current* HEAD (merge-base against HEAD, libexec/orchid-start:524); if the operator checks out a different branch between two otherwise-identical `orchid start` runs, the merge base moves and the second run can falsely refuse inherited-only task state — the failure direction is safe (refusal, no state damage) and the shape requires an operator branch switch, but it is a residual non-idempotence the recorded-fork-point alternative would not have
